steps.what: Direct and coordinate medical staff activities during patient care

tasks.design: Retain clinical team direction with the surgeon. Existing plans in {DOCS} may support coordination, but no repeated clerical component is established within the live care task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical coordination depends on the changing patient situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared plans remain available without a new system.
tasks.still_hard: Prioritising care and resolving uncertainty across the team.
tasks.human_edge: Situational awareness and accountable clinical leadership.
tasks.altitude: Clinical leadership and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Live clinical team direction requires contextual professional judgement; no task-specific labour reduction is established.

assumptions: Boundary covers direct clinical team coordination; service scheduling and procurement are separate.
Team members supply observations through existing clinical communication; the surgeon interprets them within s1. No structured acuity or availability flags are assumed.
Test native shared-plan features before custom code; no new automation is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the clinical coordination process remains unchanged.
unknowns: Whether clerical coordination is actually performed within this task
research_questions: Does observed team direction contain any separable repeat administration?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Live clinical leadership retains full time; no clerical baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Follow established surgical techniques while adapting to operative findings

tasks.design: Retain operative technique with the surgeon. Protocol material in {DOCS} supports preparation, but the physical procedure and responses to findings remain fully counted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Surgery combines physical skill with patient-specific judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operative protocols remain usable without new automation.
tasks.still_hard: Anatomical variation and unexpected operative findings.
tasks.human_edge: Direct tissue handling and accountable intraoperative decisions.
tasks.altitude: Operative responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Improve shared anticipation of operative steps

evidence.claim: Performing surgical techniques requires physical and clinical expertise; no software labour saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is following techniques during the operation; preoperative planning and postoperative reports are separate.
Surgeon obtains findings directly during s1; no structured anatomy, safety flag or automated tissue interpretation is assumed.
Consider existing protocol access before custom code; no new system or robotic intervention is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the operative process remains unchanged.
unknowns: Procedure mix and existing surgical equipment
research_questions: Is any non-operative clerical work mistakenly included in the observed technique task?

already_counted.description: Operative technique and response to findings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Physical surgery and intraoperative judgement retain full time.

steps.what: Determine procedures, service priorities, resource requirements and scheduling constraints
Calculate candidate surgery schedules against checked service constraints
Coordinate surgery services, approve schedules and arrange required supplies and equipment

tasks.design: Use native surgical scheduling features in the hospital operations system {OTHER} to calculate candidate timetables. Keep procedure choice, priority decisions, coordination and supply requests through {PROCUREMENT} with authorized staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manually moving already specified cases between available slots can consume scheduling time.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit resource and duration constraints can produce candidate schedules.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical priority, uncertain case duration and actual availability of staff and equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing patient needs and service trade-offs.
tasks.altitude: Reduce limited timetable manipulation while retaining service decisions.

evidence.claim: Explicit scheduling constraints can produce candidate timetables, but the task-specific labour saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers the surgeon's service management contribution; clinical team direction during care, patient treatment and procurement execution remain separate.

Surgeon captures case ID, procedure, priority, estimated duration, staff and equipment needs and verified slot availability in s1, including consultation and capture. No patient readiness or stock flag is assumed without human confirmation.

Existing coordinators provide resource context through normal management exchanges; no new structured reporting is imposed on them. Unconfirmed inputs or conflicts return to manual coordination in s3.
The {OTHER} slot is the hospital operations system. Test native scheduling first; already automatic date calculations and unchanged procurement work earn no saving.
unknowns: Existing scheduling automation and resource data quality
research_questions: Can candidate scheduling save surgeon time after resource verification and coordination are included?

already_counted.description: Coordination, schedule approval and supply requests

approvals.approved_version: Cases, procedures, priorities, durations, resources, schedule and requests; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross15 minus focal upkeep7 gives net8. Zero if the surgeon does not manually manipulate schedules or calculations are already automatic; clinical decisions and procurement coordination retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Order laboratory tests and imaging procedures based on the clinical question
Interpret laboratory results and diagnostic imaging in the patient's clinical context

tasks.design: Retain test selection and clinical interpretation in the patient record and imaging environment {OTHER}. No orthopedic-specific diagnostic capability or removable clerical component is established for this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test selection and interpretation require clinical reasoning.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing diagnostic results remain available through current systems.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling tests with symptoms, history and clinical uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a result changes management or needs further investigation.
tasks.altitude: Diagnostic authority and working time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify the clinical question for imaging review

evidence.claim: Orthopedic diagnostic test selection and interpretation require clinical judgement; no task-specific labour saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary covers the surgeon's ordering and interpretation; diagnostic sample collection, imaging acquisition and laboratory reporting remain outside it and unchanged.

Diagnostic teams produce results after s1 and before s2 through the existing workflow; their labour receives no saving and no new capture requirement. Missing results require normal follow-up rather than an inferred result.
The {OTHER} slot is the patient record and imaging environment. Consider native result presentation before custom code; no new automation is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the existing diagnostic workflow remains unchanged.
unknowns: Existing result presentation and diagnostic tools
research_questions: Does observed diagnostic work contain a separable repeated retrieval component?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Ordering and interpretation retain full time; diagnostic team labour and existing system runtime earn no new saving.
